title: Count Valid Substrings II
spaceBreakdown:
- int lastA, lastAB, lastABC: three scalars → O(1)
- long long ans: one scalar → O(1)
- loop index r: one scalar → O(1)
- not counted: input string s, returned value
approach: For each ending index r, a substring s[l..r] is valid (no "abc" subsequence) exactly when l is greater than the largest starting index p of any "abc" subsequence fully inside s[0..r]. We maintain three running indices while scanning left to right: the latest 'a' position (lastA), the largest start of any "ab" subsequence (lastAB), and the largest start of any "abc" subsequence (lastABC). On 'a' we update lastA; on 'b' we update lastAB = max(lastAB, lastA); on 'c' we update lastABC = max(lastABC, lastAB). At each r we add (r − lastABC) to the answer. All three start at −1 so prefixes without a complete "abc" contribute all their starting positions.
hints: For a fixed ending index r, what single quantity about the prefix s[0..r] determines how many starting indices l make s[l..r] free of "abc" as a subsequence? The string has up to 10^5 characters, so checking every (l, r) pair is too slow.

Track three running indices: latest 'a', largest start of an "ab" subsequence, and largest start of an "abc" subsequence. In "abac", at r=3 ('c') the "ab" starting at index 0 completes, so lastABC becomes 0 and only starts 1..3 are valid → add 3.

**Single character** - n = 1, no subsequence possible.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: initializing lastABC to 0 instead of -1 → returns 0

**Update order on 'c'** - the "abc" completing at this position must be counted before adding.
`Input: s = "abc"` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: adding r - lastABC to ans before updating lastABC on 'c' → returns 6

**All same characters** - no 'b' or 'c', so every substring is valid.
`Input: s = "aaa"` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: updating lastABC on every character instead of only on 'c' → returns 3

**Overflow** - n = 10^5 all 'a's gives 100000 × 100001 / 2 = 5000050000.
`Input: s = "a" repeated 100000 times` → `Expected: 5000050000`
⚠️ Bug: using int for ans → returns 705082704 (signed overflow wrap)

followUps.q: Generalize the forbidden subsequence to an arbitrary string t of length k over any alphabet. How does the approach scale?
followUps.a: Maintain k running indices tracking the largest start of each prefix of t as a subsequence. On a character matching t[i], update index i from index i−1. Time O(n·k), space O(k).

followUps.q: Instead of counting substrings avoiding "abc", count those containing "abc" as a subsequence.
followUps.a: Subtract the valid count from n(n+1)/2. Equivalently, at each r add lastABC + 1 instead of r − lastABC. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: The string arrives as a stream of unknown length; answer queries asking for the running count after each new character.
followUps.a: The three indices and running total update in O(1) per character, so emit ans after each append. Time O(1) amortized per query, space O(1).
